clue.text: Order cheap rubbish after joke backfired

indicators.note: something that backfires comes back the way it went, so the letters run the other way
after means following, so the piece before this word in the clue goes second in the answer

blocks.note: to kid is to joke or tease
tat is cheap, tasteless goods

explanation.surface: Someone orders cheap rubbish after a practical joke goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the rubbish second, so the reversed joke comes first. Tat is British slang for tawdry junk.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is a harsh decree imposed without consultation, a kind of command handed down.

clue.text: Vilified when raised to be free

blocks.note: to revile is to vilify or abuse verbally

indicators.note: something on the outside wraps round what it holds, so one piece surrounds another

M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.walkthrough: 10 is PRESUMABLY, the theme: each such answer is a word you might presume exists because its negative does. 12 is SHEVELED, the presumed opposite of dishevelled, so '10 12' is presumably tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkempt means untidy, so the presumed positive form describes hair or dress that is neat and combed.

clue.text: Offend when taking note of clothes

explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is only a joiner; the note sits inside the word for offend, before its final L.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal or trade word for garments and clothing in general.

clue.text: Paracetamol is helping part get erect 10

explanation.walkthrough: 10 is PRESUMABLY: to demolish is to knock down, so the presumed un-negated verb would be to put up.
explanation.definitionFit: Demolish means knock down a building, so its imagined opposite means to build or put up a structure.

clue.text: In Latin, opera works

blocks.note: first meaning: the Latin plural of opus is opera, so opera in Latin means this
second meaning: pieces of music or other creative compositions

explanation.surface: Opera works composed in Latin, like a sacred oratorio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opera' looks like the art form; here it is the Latin plural of opus, whose English plural is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus means a composition, particularly a numbered musical one, and the English plural adds -es to the singular.

clue.text: Nasty and nice, so soon

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is nasty and nice by turns, and so quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty and nice' looks like a pair of opposite adjectives; the first is the signal, and 'so' belongs to the letters too.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means very shortly or in a moment, a colloquial way of saying before long.

clue.text: Shelley knew endless Greek

blocks.note: the poet's name without its first and last letters
the word without its first and last letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' applies to both words before it, trimming each at front and back.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hellene is a native of Greece, from Hellas, the Greeks' own name for their country.

clue.text: Primarily means a national darling ending longstanding apartheid's prior hold

definitions.text: Primarily means a national darling ending longstanding apartheid's prior hold

indicators.note: prior says coming before, so one piece is placed ahead of the rest
primarily says first of all, so only the opening letter of each word counts

blocks.note: a nelson is a wrestling hold with the arm under the opponent's and the hand on the neck

blocks.clueFragment: means a national darling ending longstanding apartheid's
blocks.note: the initial letters of seven words

explanation.surface: A tribute to a national darling who ended long-standing apartheid.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: the initials spell the surname and the wrestling hold gives the first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandela, South Africa's beloved first black president, led the struggle that ended decades of racial segregation there.

clue.text: Desirable fruit

blocks.note: first meaning: much sought after, as in a choice job
second meaning: a sweet stone fruit

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like one phrase about tempting fruit; they are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it describes a choice position or role; as a noun it names an oval purple stone fruit.

clue.text: One might expect a plumber's work to have a messy end

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or shape it, so the letters get reshaped
an end is the final point, so only the closing letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
taken as written
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: You would expect a plumber's job to end in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' reads as the plumber's job, but it is the signal to rework the letters. This answer is the theme: several clues use 10 to mean a word you might presume exists.
explanation.definitionFit: Presumably means it is reasonable to suppose, which is what saying someone could anticipate a thing conveys.

clue.text: Democrat available to frame up image

indicators.note: a frame surrounds a picture, so the words surround the letters wanted
going up is going backwards, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the letters bridging the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A Democrat politician is ready to be photographed for a publicity image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is a down-clue reversal signal, used loosely in an across clue to mean read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An avatar is a graphic figure representing a user online, or an embodiment, so a picture standing for someone.

clue.text: Had empty sleeve tailored to be tidy 10 across the pond

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its inside, leaving only its outer letters
tailored cloth is cut and restitched, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first and last letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone had an empty sleeve altered so they'd look tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across the pond' means American: US spelling uses one L in disheveled, so the presumed positive has one L too.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishevelled means untidy, so the presumed opposite describes someone neat and well groomed, spelt the American way.

clue.text: Audible drivel you provided, temporarily drunk

indicators.note: audible means heard, so the word is taken for its sound not its spelling

blocks.note: crap is vulgar slang for nonsense
the letter U is pronounced like the pronoun
to lend is to provide something for a limited time

explanation.surface: Someone talks audible drivel, having been temporarily drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temporarily' belongs with 'provided', not with 'drunk': the definition is the last word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Crapulent is a rare word for intoxicated or suffering the after-effects of too much alcohol.

clue.text: Chef beginning to stuff little French onion, must be peeled and loaded 10

indicators.note: a beginning is the start, so only the opening letter is taken
stuffing puts something inside, so one piece is packed into another

the first letter
the word without its first and last letters
the word without its first and last letters

explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for wealthy, and the imagined opposite of impecunious (having no money) would mean moneyed.

clue.text: Missing family is OK at last, with the paramedic team, getting treatment

indicators.note: at last means at the end, so only the final letter of each word is kept
treatment works on something and changes it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the final letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A patient pining for family is doing fine at last, being treated by paramedics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'OK at last' tempts you to take just K; 'at last' works on the four words after it instead, and OK is used whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Being homesick is longing for home and relatives while away, so missing one's family describes it exactly.

clue.text: See 15
Skinhead, if true, got drunk to excess

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an oversupply or overindulgence, too much of something, especially food or drink.

clue.text: Straight battle: the odds leave one standing

indicators.note: when the odd-numbered letters go, only the second, fourth and sixth letters remain

blocks.note: candid means frank or straight-talking
the even-numbered letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Straight battle' suggests a straight fight between two; 'the odds' sounds like betting odds but means letters 1, 3 and 5.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate stands for election, so one who is running for office is someone standing.

clue.text: Soundly immersed, time flies

blocks.note: dipped means immersed, and this spelling says it the same way
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Deeply absorbed in something, you find that time flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly immersed' reads as deeply absorbed, and 'time flies' as the proverb; 'flies' is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Diptera is the insect order of two-winged true flies, including houseflies, mosquitoes and gnats.

clue.text: 10 calm, if instructed to keep right

explanation.walkthrough: 10 is PRESUMABLY: distraught means very upset, so the presumed positive would mean composed.
explanation.definitionFit: Distraught means frantic with worry, so its imagined undoing describes someone serene and untroubled.

clue.text: De janvier, peut-être, la fille devient jeune dame

explanation.definitionFit: Demoiselle is an old or literary word for a young unmarried woman, a damsel, which jeune dame translates.

the first letter
